subject.title: fix(clickclack): add timeouts to REST client requests

question: Should every ClickClack REST operation unconditionally fail after 30 seconds, including existing installations whose service may respond more slowly?
rationale: The patch replaces an unbounded wait with a new behavioral default, but no ClickClack service contract or live proof establishes that 30 seconds is safe for every supported REST method.

options.title: Accept the 30-second deadline
options.body: Treat 30 seconds as the supported ClickClack REST boundary, document it in the PR context, and require live timeout proof before merge.

options.title: Adjust from service evidence
options.body: Choose a different fixed deadline based on the ClickClack API's documented or observed maximum latency, without adding new user configuration.

options.title: Pause for contract proof
options.body: Keep the PR open until the ClickClack service owner or live validation establishes an appropriate deadline.

recommendation.title: Accept the 30-second deadline
recommendation.body: Treat 30 seconds as the supported ClickClack REST boundary, document it in the PR context, and require live timeout proof before merge.
